source.title: TAN without a burn: Scaling Laws of DP-SGD
source.authors: Tom Sander; Pierre Stock; Alexandre Sablayrolles

record.tranche_reason: Tests how batch size relates to held-out accuracy in DP-SGD training, a new setting for the batch-size claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports batch-size scaling results for test accuracy. It does not report the training-to-test error gap, and its batch comparisons use DP-SGD at fixed steps and fixed per-step signal-to-noise ratio.
record.test_reason: Appendix B reports an optimizer comparison bearing on V4 in noisy, differentially private ImageNet training. The recorded batch-size comparisons do not test V5's fixed-epoch claim: steps are fixed, so increasing batch size increases epochs, while the noise multiplier also changes.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the batch-scaling findings and identifies stochasticity as a hypothesis rather than an established explanation. The paper's broader conclusion is that TAN enables inexpensive hyperparameter search and improved private ImageNet accuracy. It also reports SGD without momentum outperforming the adaptive optimizers tested.
record.recipe_differences: Uses DP-SGD with clipped gradients and added Gaussian noise; batch comparisons hold steps and per-step signal-to-noise ratio constant.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and batch size; CIFAR-10 and ImageNet show different batch-scaling patterns.

fits_no_version.finding: CIFAR-10 test accuracy stays nearly constant and ImageNet accuracy decreases as batches grow at fixed steps and fixed per-step signal-to-noise ratio.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under TAN scaling in noisy training, batch-size effects on test accuracy depend on the dataset even when update count and injected update-noise scale are held constant.

fits_no_version.finding: NF-ResNet-50 performs best, classical ResNets are intermediate, and ViTs perform worst in the architecture simulations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture affects ImageNet accuracy under noisy, step-constrained training; this comparison does not establish a convolutional advantage over fully connected networks.

record.problems: The relevant batch-size comparisons are in DP-SGD rather than standard non-private training, hold steps rather than epochs fixed, and report test accuracy rather than the train-test error gap. Figure 4 shows the values; the text describes the trends but does not give the per-batch numbers.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization in the same architectures and recipes.
Width scaling beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks, local connectivity, and initialization transfer.

The restricted learning-rate-and-schedule tuning protocol; training-performance comparisons; non-private benchmarks; language models; and switching from Adam to SGD. AdamW was tried, but its separate effect is not reported.
Fixed-epoch batch-size comparisons and whether recipe adaptations remove a penalty under that budget.
Dropout effects and interactions with training-set size, augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

missing.what: Optimizer comparison: SGD with no momentum and constant learning rate is reported best across tested architectures after exploring Adam and AdamW over a wide parameter range. Add rows capturing the textual ranking; numerical optimizer accuracies and the adaptive-optimizer search ranges are not supplied.
missing.locator: Section 4.2, Choice of architecture and optimizer; Appendix B, Optimizer

record.verdict_notes: Absence of a train-test gap does not itself disqualify evidence for V4 or V5, which name held-out performance. The decisive mismatch for R1 and R2 is the training-budget protocol. Broad optimizer tuning does not establish V4's restricted-tuning condition, but the reported optimizer ranking bears on V4 in a new setting.

versions.untested_parts: Width scaling past the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization under the stated tuning conditions.
Fixed epoch budgets; non-private training; language models; training-to-test error gap; the effects of longer training, learning-rate scaling with warmup, normalization or regularization changes.
Dropout effects and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: 16-4-WideResNets
rows.operation_detail: Compared batch sizes at constant per-step signal-to-noise ratio and number of steps.
rows.value: The paper states performance is almost constant for various levels of noise on CIFAR-10; Figure 4 gives figure-only values.
rows.note: Comparison is at fixed steps and per-step signal-to-noise ratio, not a fixed epoch budget; no training error or train-test gap is reported.
rows.check: Fixed steps and constant noise-to-batch ratio cannot establish V5's fixed-epoch effect. The reported nearly constant accuracy is valid for this different comparison. Augmentation is specified: Section 4.1 says Augmentation Multiplicity is always used.

source_check.correct: Section 4.1 specifies augmentation multiplicity for both datasets; the augmentation type and multiplicity used specifically in Figure 4 are not stated.
source_check.locator_found: Section 4, Batch Scaling Laws; Figure 4 left panel and caption; Section 4.1, Experimental Setup.
source_check.problem: The augmentation condition omits the general specification of augmentation multiplicity.

rows.subject: NF-ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Compared batch sizes at constant per-step signal-to-noise ratio across several step counts.
rows.value: The paper states accuracy (log) linearly decreases with batch size; Figure 4 gives figure-only values.
rows.note: The reported decline is for DP-SGD at fixed steps and per-step signal-to-noise ratio, not a fixed epoch budget; no training error or train-test gap is reported.
rows.check: The ImageNet accuracy decline is explicitly reported, but fixed steps and changing noise multiplier do not test V5's fixed-epoch comparison. Calling it partial confuses a different experimental condition with an incomplete effect.
